jobs.title: Sr. Director, Enterprise Finance Systems
jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Your Impact

As Senior Director, Finance Systems within OpenText’s CDO organization, you’ll have the opportunity to shape how technology enables Finance at a global scale. This is a highly visible leadership role where you’ll lead functional and technical teams responsible for Finance systems delivery, operations, and modernization, including SAP on-premises applications and integrated services.

You’ll help drive OpenText’s Finance modernization agenda, including the implementation of S/4HANA Cloud, while partnering with senior Finance and IT leaders to turn business priorities into technology outcomes. You’ll lead through complexity, leverage AI and emerging technologies, and deliver measurable value for Finance teams and business users globally.

What You Will Do

Work closely with senior leaders to understand business objectives and develop the finance systems roadmap.
Responsible for leading the team in the delivery, operational support and continuous improvement of the SAP on-premises applications.
Finance modernization including the implementation of S/4HANA Cloud capabilities and the broader ecosystem of solutions integrated into SAP
Work with Architecture and rest of the peer network to develop and maintain Financial Systems Landscape relevance.
Accountable for delivery of change & bug-fixes for all finance Systems
Accountable for the operational upkeep of the finance systems including SOX and other IT general controls.
Accountable for people agenda for the finance systems team.
Key contributor to the overall technology delivery strategy, ensuring the realization of goals such as reuse, infrastructure simplification, cost management, solution flexibility, operational resilience and the practical use of emerging technologies, including AI, to solve outcome-driven business and IT use cases.
Build strong cross-organizational relationships and effectively influence staff across the business and IT.

What You Are Great At

Building strong relationships and effectively managing expectations with senior stakeholders, business partners, peers, and external vendors.
Breaking down complex business problems into practical technology solutions, including automation and AI, to deliver measurable business and IT outcomes.
Leading effectively in a global operating model, with teams distributed across geographies and organizational structures.
Communicating complex technical and business concepts clearly and effectively to leadership and diverse audiences.
Thinking strategically and critically, developing roadmaps, and translating strategy into execution.
Managing multiple priorities, plans, and budgets in a fast-paced environment while delivering on time and on budget.
Driving best practices, continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and a culture of learning across teams.
Building and motivating high-performing teams and fostering an environment of trust, collaboration, and accountability.

What It Takes To Excel

10+ years of experience leading engineering, development, or technology delivery teams.
Strong experience leading complex SAP ERP delivery and operations, including SAP on-premises platforms and integrated Finance systems.
Proven experience leading S/4HANA Cloud implementations, including program delivery, business process transformation, stakeholder alignment, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization.
Strong understanding of complementary financial systems and cross-domain technology ecosystems, including Finance, HR, and CRM.
Experience supporting technology integrations related to Mergers, Acquisitions, and Divestitures (M&A).
Experience leading multiple complex workstreams within a global organization.
High-tech software or technology services industry experience is an asset.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a relevant discipline, college diploma, or equivalent experience.

One Last Thing:
If you’re a strategic technology leader who thrives on transformation, enjoys solving complex business challenges, and wants to shape the future of Finance technology at a global scale, we’d love to hear from you.

OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a ticket at Ask HR. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.

Compensation:
At OpenText, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your physical, emotional, and financial wellbeing. As you move through the hiring process, we’re happy to provide more details about our compensation programs, including variable and commission compensation opportunities for eligible roles, vacation entitlement, and paid time off.

Salary Range:
Depending on the candidate’s education, experience, skills, geographical location, and alignment with internal equity and external market, actual salary may vary and be higher or lower than the range posted.

AI Usage Disclosure:
As part of our commitment to transparency, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in various stages of our recruitment process, including resume screening, candidate matching, interview scheduling, and communications. These tools are designed to improve efficiency, reduce bias, and enhance candidate experience. All decisions regarding hiring are made by qualified human professionals, and we continuously monitor our AI systems to ensure fairness and compliance with applicable regulations.

jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Product Management
jobs.description:
Job Description

Senior Director, AI Product Management

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader who can turn a strategic product vision into shipped reality at scale. As Senior Director, AI Product Management, you will own user-focused product success for RBC's internal Agentic AI platform, defining the product vision and translating it into a tangible roadmap, community, and ecosystem. You will build discipline around ensuring relentless customer focus and a business-strategy lens on what we build and why. You will lead a team of Product Managers and own Voice of the Customer, feature prioritization, adoption and community building around the product across RBC.

You will be expected to set the operating rhythm, make the hard tradeoff and resourcing calls, and hold a quality bar — bringing the credibility that comes from having built and shipped AI products at scale, not just managed roadmaps.

Your responsibilities will include:

Team leadership: Leading and developing Director-level leads (across Product Strategy & Roadmap, Community & Adoption, Ecosystem & Partnerships) and the teams beneath them, with clear career paths and succession
Integrated delivery: Owning a single execution plan that aligns roadmap delivery, community programs, and partnership milestones to one cadence
Operating cadence: Establishing and running sprint reviews, quarterly planning, and OKR setting and tracking
Tradeoff and escalation ownership: Serving as the primary escalation point for cross-pillar dependencies, tradeoffs, and resourcing decisions
Product quality: Maintaining acceptance criteria, release gates, and documentation standards across the squad
Adoption and outcomes: Using analytics, telemetry, and adoption measurement to drive decisions and report progress, risks, and resource needs
Ecosystem health: Ensuring the community and partnership programs sustain engagement and healthy adoption across the RBC user base

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading multi-team product organizations as a manager of managers
Have a track record of customer discovery and translating user needs into product strategy and prioritization
Have hands-on experience delivering end-user facing AI products — ideally generative or agentic AI — at production scale
Have run large-scale internal or enterprise product launches with measurable adoption outcomes
Bring strong operational discipline: agile delivery, OKR frameworks, and release management
Are data-driven, comfortable with analytics, telemetry, and adoption metrics as the basis for product decisions
Have financial services experience, or the ability to rapidly develop it - understanding how banking employees work and the regulatory constraints on internal tooling
Have a working knowledge of LLM evaluation, prompt engineering, or RAG architecture — sufficient to shape product decisions and engage technical teams

Nice to have:

MBA or Master's in a technical or business discipline
Product management certification (CSPO, SAFe, AIPM, or Pragmatic Institute)
Background in platform engineering or developer experience teams
Experience in a major bank's technology or digital transformation function

What's in it for you:

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC
Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

Inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment

RBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We are pleased to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veterans status, Aboriginal/Native American status or any other legally-protected factors. Disability-related accommodations during the application process are available upon request.

Big Data Analytics, Client Counseling, Coaching Others, Critical Thinking, Decision Making, Industry Knowledge, Machine Learning (ML), Results-Oriented, Software Engineering, Software Product Design

jobs.title: Director, Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR)
jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

Reporting to the AVP, Accounting & Controls, the Director, Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR) is responsible for leading the Canadian ICOFR program and ensuring the organization maintains a sustainable, risk-based, and effective control environment.

The Director serves as the central point of coordination across Canada Finance, Business, Technology, Risk & Controls, Internal Audit, and External Audit, providing governance and oversight over the design, evaluation, remediation, and continuous improvement of internal controls that support reliable financial reporting and CEO/CFO certification requirements.

This role is a key leadership position within the Canada Controller Group, responsible for driving control effectiveness, remediation governance, continuous improvement, and the overall maturity of the Canadian control environment.

What You Will Be Doing

Governance & Program Oversight: Lead the Canadian ICOFR program by providing governance and oversight that supports CEO/CFO certification requirements, coordinating across Canada Finance, Business, Technology, Risk & Controls, Internal Audit, and External Audit, and delivering timely reporting, insights, and recommendations to senior management
Control Design & Operating Effectiveness Oversight: Provide oversight of the design, documentation, assessment, and continuous improvement of the Canadian control environment through risk assessment and scoping activities, quality reviews, consistent application of ICOFR methodologies, and control optimization initiatives
Deficiency Evaluation & Remediation Oversight: Provide Canada-wide governance over control deficiency assessments and remediation activities, including severity evaluation, remediation oversight, progress monitoring, and validation of remediation outcomes. Communicate ICOFR assessments, remediation status, emerging risks, and key conclusions to senior management
Enhancing the Overall Control Environment: Lead the evolution of the Canadian control environment by identifying opportunities to strengthen processes and controls, enhancing the quality and consistency of control documentation, promoting stronger control ownership and accountability across the organization, and providing education and guidance to support control awareness
Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team by providing coaching, mentorship, and development opportunities, while fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and business partnership

What You Will Bring

CPA designation (required)
8+ years of progressive experience in internal controls, external audit, internal audit, or financial reporting, including experience leading teams, complex initiatives, and cross-functional stakeholder groups
Strong knowledge of internal control frameworks, including COSO and Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR/SOX), with experience evaluating control deficiencies, remediation activities, and financial reporting impacts
Demonstrated experience leading ICOFR, control optimization, remediation, or control automation initiatives
Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment
Exceptional communication, presentation, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and business partners
Proven experience building, coaching, and leading high-performing teams; experience within the insurance or financial services industry is a strong asset

Given the size and scope of our organization, we have the flexibility for this position to be located in the following head office locations: Toronto, London, Winnipeg. This role follows a hybrid work model, with an in-office presence required three days per week.

The base salary for this position is between $128,200 - $178,200
annually. This represents base salary only and does not represent other variable compensation components of our total compensation ( i.e. annual bonus, commission etc). If you are selected to move forward in our recruitment process, your recruiter will be able to discuss additional details of our total rewards program with you.

Career opportunities will be open a minimum of 5 business days from the date of posting, closing dates will vary depending on the search activity. All applications received will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Grow with Canada Life

We’re united by a shared purpose: to improve the financial, physical and mental well-being of Canadians. Our company is trusted by 1 in 3 Canadians and contributes to the strength of communities across the country.

We’re looking for people who live our values everyday: we step up, we do the right thing, and we deliver – for our customers, communities and each other. Are you someone who always strives to do the right thing, who steps up for themselves and others, and who delivers with impact? Then we want to hear from you!

What we offer
:

We’re committed to supporting our employees through every stage of their career. Here’s what you can expect as a full-time or part-time permanent team member:

Career Development: Opportunities for career advancement, access to industry-leading learning programs and up to $2,000 annually towards education reimbursement.
Health & Wellness: Flexible health and dental benefits, plus a $5,000 mental health benefit to support your well-being.
Time Off: In addition to regular vacation and personal days, we support community involvement with a volunteer day. 
Financial Security: Company-matching pension plan, share ownership program and additional investment options.
Rewards and Recognition: Employee recognition programs, service milestone celebrations, employee discounts and more!
Emphasis on Community: We provide a workplace where employees feel connected and supported through Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), mentorship programs, social clubs and events.

Learn more about Canada Life.

We’re committed to removing barriers and ensuring equal access to employment. Applicants requiring reasonable accommodation during the application process may contact talentacquisitioncanada@canadalife.com . All information provided will be handled in accordance with applicable laws and Canada Life policies.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Reporting
jobs.description:
SETUP
: Mostly remote, only required 1-2 times/month in office. Located in North York, ON

CONTRACT
: 18 months

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4–5 finance and accounting professionals, establishing clear responsibilities and development priorities.
Provide technical guidance and oversight to the team while promoting accountability and high-quality execution.
Partner closely with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and other finance functions to ensure consistency and accuracy across financial reporting.
Work with senior leadership to communicate financial reporting matters, accounting implications, and significant issues.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities, and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and reporting perspective.

Process Improvement:
Drive improvements to the financial close, consolidation, and reporting processes with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reconciliation activities.
Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

About You

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
Strong technical knowledge and practical application of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Significant experience with multi-entity consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency considerations.
Experience leading and developing accounting or financial reporting teams.

307950.

This position for employment is for a current vacancy with Vaco/Highspring’s client. You must currently reside within the Greater Toronto area and be permitted to work in Canada to be considered for this opportunity. A recruiter will be in touch with you if your profile meets our client’s requirements for this role.

Determining compensation for this role (and others) at Vaco/Highspring depends upon a wide array of factors including but not limited to the individual’s skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, office location and other geographic considerations, as well as other business and organizational needs. With that said, as required by local law in geographies that require salary range disclosure, Vaco/Highspring notes the salary range for the role is noted in this job posting. The individual may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses, and can participate in medical, dental, and vision benefits as well as the company’s 401(k) retirement plan.
